outline.summary: Chapter opens with Baldwin Dictionary + Encyclopaedia Britannica characterizations of idealism, recoded as the philosophical school that features Agent — ego, self, super-ego, consciousness, will, generalized I, mind, spirit, oversoul, and the 'super-persons' (church, race, nation) — as motive-locus. Esthetic-idealist cluster (sensibility, expression, self-expression, unconscious) introduced as the bridge between metaphysical and aesthetic idealism, with Henry James's preface to Portrait of a Lady as paradigm of book-as-act-grounded-in-author's-mind-as-motivating-scene.

Sociological invitation to idealism: when economic relations get 'idealized' or 'spiritualized.' Greek 'Moira' as case study — drift from realistic-distributive (one's portion, share) to idealistic-fatalistic (Destiny). Plato's Republic answers Sophistic relativism of dike with an ideal Justice as unifying remoter term; dialectical move = adoption of broader term to encompass conflicting concretes. Law-court idealization invites both legal-idealist construction and materialist-debunker decoding.

Idealism's powerfully creative aspect: the ideal as standard / guide / incentive (Washington, Lenin, Shelley, Coleridge's poetry as 'dim analogue of Creation'); written-contract idealization; corporation-as-person legal fiction as case study in agent-extension. Positive law masks idealism: Rousseau's volonté générale + US fiction of consubstantial founder-will-with-present-will = idealistic-agent ground for legal motive.

Realism-plus-money-equals-idealism as cultural law. Money introduces a new spiritualizing term into barter; technology compounds the same effect by demanding the unifying function of ideas/ideals and by raising knowledge (epistemology) to philosophical pre-eminence. Emerson's Nature passage on the poet who 'owns the horizon' as paradigmatic idealistic-unification image.

Berkeley as representative idealist — Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge as the clearest exhibit of idealist terminology, equally clean as Hobbes was for materialist terminology. Burke's exegetical move: Berkeley begins psychologistically (questioning abstract ideas as Locke defined them), reduces all sensible objects to ideas (esse is percipi), reduces 'matter' itself to unnecessary hypothesis, anchors active principle in mind/spirit/soul, and routes the residual scene-function through 'God' as 'Almighty Agent' — i.e., scene-translated-into-terms-of-agent. The very strategy is itself the operationalization of Agent as featured term.

Hume as the transitional figure who NARROWS Berkeleian idealism's circumference: by equating 'ideas' with 'sensations' he drops the rationalist/intelligible side of the equation, focuses on what laboratory investigation can handle, and dismantles causality/power/necessary connection as empirically un-derivable. The 'great dramatist cluster' (reason, substance, cause, necessity, action, idea, God, Nature, generation, power) begins to fall apart. Symbolic-level reading: Hume's 'placid bachelor' position as questioning of potency-and-progeny.

Leibniz's monadology as agent-featuring rationalism that anticipates modern psychologies of the unconscious. Monads = atom-agents, each with own internal principle of self-development from implicit to explicit; pre-established harmony = deus-ex-machina device that produces co-development without inter-monadic windows; God as Monas Monadum unifying infinite-points-of-view plurality. Leibniz idealizes substance toward perception (vs. scholastic substance-toward-action), preparing the ground for Kant's encounter with both Leibnizian unification and Humean skepticism.

Burke's constructive reconstruction of Kantian terminology as a response to Hume's demand for a 'medium': equate the medium with the very nature of the agent itself. Universalize agent (not 'your understanding' or 'mine' but 'the understanding'); split universal agent into passive (sensibility, receives intuitions) and active (understanding, performs unification by concepts); locate categories transcendentally in the agent rather than in objects. The 'transcendental' as the conditions-of-the-possibility-of-knowledge inside agent rather than in scene. Result so far: a scene-with-circumference-narrowed-to-motion derived from a function of agent — neither materialism nor supernaturalism.

The third Critique-move: desynonymize 'transcendental' (the conditions on appearance) and 'transcendent' (the realm of things-in-themselves, of unconditioned, of freedom). Burke borrows the desynonymizing maneuver from Coleridge's Biographia Literaria (imaginatio/phantasia → imagination/fancy). The transcendent realm = realm of things-without-context, realm of unconditioned, hence of freedom; allows for moral action ('I must abolish knowledge to make room for belief'); intelligible re-defined as that-which-cannot-be-sensed; phenomena/noumena pair; 'als ob' regulative principle linking necessity and freedom; ideas of God / freedom / immortality as bond between caused realm and first-cause realm. Constitution-enactment analogy as Burke's gloss on freedom-necessity bridge.

Fichte abolishes the thing-in-itself as unnecessary, grounds system wholly in Ego/Non-Ego, returning to Berkeleian pattern. Symbolic-level Nichtich/nichtig pun. Schelling (aesthetic), Hegel (optimistic), Schopenhauer (pessimistic) trace genealogy of objective-world from subjective, treating nature as externalization/embodiment/incarnation of spirit. Pattern: idealism-pure-and-simple = subjective-genealogy-of-the-objective. Schopenhauer's externalizations-as-compulsion-neuroses anticipate post-Schopenhauer depth-psychology.

Critical hybridity move: Marxian dialectical materialism grows out of idealism BY ANTITHESIS — Marx materialistically reverses Hegel's genealogy (matter as prius; consciousness/reason/sensation derivative). Yet because Marxism is DIALECTICAL not vulgar materialism, and because key terms are traced from scene with 'good Grammar,' there must remain 'some quality of agenthood permeating the scene itself' (Lenin: property similar to sensation in foundation stones of matter). Hence Marxism is best translated as 'idealistic materialist': futuristic stress on social unification + constant call upon human agents = intensely idealistic. The Marxist 'class' is the agent-locus.

World History = development of Spirit from potentiality to realization via embodiment in concrete historical detail. Stage-biographical analogy (Oriental childhood → Greek adolescence → Roman manhood → German old-age-as-perfect-maturity). Each State contains contradictions that drive its expansion, contact with external factors, betrayal, decay, and handing-on of spiritual-progress to next stage in different geographical theatre. 'Cunning of Reason' = Spirit acting through subjective human passions; private aims unconsciously carry out Universal design. State = highest embodiment of Spirit, 'Divine Idea as it exists on earth.' World-Historical Hero (Alexander, Caesar, Napoleon) as agent close to fountainhead of Spirit.

The Manifesto as constitution — not merely a regulative platform but soundly constitutive, grounding political principles in statements about universal scene (a scene narrowed to naturalistic limits and defined by laws of human history). The class-struggle dialectic: history = history of class struggles; oppressor/oppressed dyad → uninterrupted antagonism → revolutionary reconstitution or common ruin. Manifesto contains ~15 scenic references treating consciousness as reflection of conditions; yet the document itself, AS act of propaganda, presupposes ideas as social forces and conditions-changers. Tension between scenic-reflection rhetoric and act-of-propaganda performance held throughout.

Burke's tentative reconstruction of Marxism in act-featuring terms. Each social class distinct in actus, hence in status, hence in properties. Idea is 'active' insofar as 'adequate' (correctly names the malign/benign properties of society); society suffers social 'passions' insofar as ideas inadequate; ruling class's inadequate ideas amplify society-wide passion. Revolutionary act = transformation of class-passion into class-action under guidance of party-as-class-within-class with adequate ideas. Post-revolutionary new status; new common actus → new common status; new properties → new conditions. Spinozist alignment 'class-angled' on Marxist class-consciousness, modified by recognition of partly-active partly-unconscious character.

Materialism-grown-out-of-German-transcendentalism, parallel-to-but-different-from Marxist materialism. Skepticism-then-animal-faith move: extending doubt yields 'we see what we see' (intuitions of essences); animal-faith posits material world. Four realms: matter, essence, spirit, truth. Essence = appearance considered in itself, infinity of eternal possibilities, 'indelible background.' Avicebron's scribe-script-scroll variant: scroll = realm of essence, script-and-scribe combined = narrow text selected by existence as 're-agent.' Santayana's essences uncompromisingly individual (not familial-generative Platonic Forms); spiritual delight in essence = benign contemplation of death (thanatopsis); culmination-as-termination.

Modern cult of imagination (poetry-against-science) ironically inherits idealist-scientist patterning via Coleridge from Kant. Wallace Stevens essay (Sewanee Review autumn 1944) deployed as exhibit: imagination clusters with personality, indirect egotism, nervous sensitiveness, temperament, sensation — the idealist agent-cluster. Stevens places imagination in dialectical opposition to reason (going beyond Coleridge's imagination:fancy::reason:understanding). Shelley's poetry-as-centre-and-circumference-of-knowledge traced backward through Leibniz to Pascal to Rabelais, charting the figure's gradual scientist turn. Caution: scientist 'heresy' operating undetected in theories of poetic action.

concepts.label: Agent as motive-locus / locus of motive
concepts.gloss: The pentad term that idealism features as the originating ground from which motive proceeds — the constituting subject (mind, ego, consciousness, will). Answers the question 'Who?' (and its derivatives: by which mind? in which consciousness?).

concepts.label: Idealism features-as-locus Agent
concepts.gloss: Burke's diagnostic move: idealism is recognized as the school that treats motive as arising from the constituting subject, regardless of which particular agent-vocabulary (ego, self, super-ego, soul, spirit, mind, oversoul, super-person) it deploys.

concepts.label: Super-agent / super-person
concepts.gloss: Idealism's generalization of individual agent into collective or transcendent agents — church, race, nation, communal Ego (Fichte), Spirit (Hegel), class (Marxism), historical period treated as 'personality.' Burke: 'super-persons' are typical indicators of idealism.

concepts.label: Constituting subject (Kantian sense)
concepts.gloss: The universalized agent (not your-understanding or mine but 'the understanding') whose categories supply conditions of possibility of experience. Burke recasts as: agent-as-medium, locating in agent what materialism locates in scene.

concepts.label: Idealization / spiritualization
concepts.gloss: The drift by which a concrete-realistic term (one's portion, lot, share, justice as dike, contract) acquires an abstract-transcending sense (Destiny, ideal Justice, written-and-legally-fictional contract). Sociologically invited by disunity that calls for unification.

concepts.label: Unification (as idealist function)
concepts.gloss: The function of an ideal/idea to draw disunity into a higher-order term that encompasses the dispersed concretes (Plato's ideal Justice over Sophistic justices; nationalism over tribal disunity; Reason as ground of all existence in Kant). 'Unification' presupposes a not-yet-unity; hence its gerundive futurity.

concepts.label: Esse is percipi (to-be-is-to-be-perceived)
concepts.gloss: Berkeley's foundational equation — translatable in Burke's idiom as 'to be is to be grounded in the term super-agent,' since unperceived ideas persist by being maintained in the mind of God.

concepts.label: God as Almighty Agent / ultimate scene as super-agent
concepts.gloss: Berkeley's resolution of the scenic remainder — what materialism would call ultimate scene gets translated, in idealism, into terms of super-agent. Burke's diagnostic gloss: 'God is Berkeley's equivalent for the ultimate scene, scene as translated into terms of agent.'

concepts.label: Medium as agent (Kant's solution to Hume)
concepts.gloss: Hume demanded a 'medium' to explain the inference from observed-sequence to causal-necessity; Burke shows Kant equating this medium with the universalized agent itself, transforming the problem into a solution by relocating causality from scene to agent's nature.

concepts.label: Transcendental vs. empirical (scene-narrowed-to-motion)
concepts.gloss: Kantian distinction: the empirical realm of objects-as-conditioned by the transcendental forms (space, time, categories) yields a 'scene with circumference narrowed to the scope of motion,' derived from a function of agent. Mechanistic determinism with no room for action.

concepts.label: Desynonymize (Coleridgean strategic operation)
concepts.gloss: The operation, named by Coleridge in Biographia Literaria, of making a distinction-in-kind between two formerly synonymous terms (imaginatio/phantasia → imagination/fancy). Burke generalizes: great departures in thought turn synonyms into opposites or vice versa. Kant's transcendental/transcendent split is paradigm.

concepts.label: Transcendent realm / unconditioned / freedom
concepts.gloss: Kant's realm of things-in-themselves, things-without-context — Grammatically the realm of the unconditioned, hence of freedom, hence of the possibility of moral action. Cannot be known; can be thought.

concepts.label: Als ob (regulative 'as if')
concepts.gloss: Kantian principle bridging realm of necessity and realm of freedom: we cannot know there are God, freedom, and immortality, but we ought to act as if there were. Ideas of God / freedom / immortality as moral motive.

concepts.label: Ego / Non-Ego (Fichtean abolition of thing-in-itself)
concepts.gloss: Fichte's collapse of Kant's thing-in-itself into a Non-Ego derived from the Ego — returning idealism to the Berkeleian terminus where agent is the unique principle, with Symbolic-level Nichtich/nichtig undertone.

concepts.label: Cunning of Reason (Hegelian)
concepts.gloss: Hegel's mechanism: Spirit acts through individual human passions; private agents pursuing private ends unconsciously carry out the Will of Providence / World History's design. Bridges the gap between subjective-individual and universal-Spirit by making the subjective the medium of the universal.

concepts.label: Class as collective agent (Marxist hybrid)
concepts.gloss: Despite materialist surface vocabulary, Marxism's motive-locus is the CLASS as collective agent: futuristic stress on social unification + constant call upon human agents + class as bearer of properties and consciousness = Agent-featuring at the structural level. Burke: dialectical materialism is best translated as 'idealistic materialist.'

concepts.label: Agenthood permeating scene (Lenin)
concepts.gloss: Lenin's move (Materialism and Empirio-Criticism) to attribute to matter itself 'a property similar to sensation in the foundation stones of the structure of matter itself' — preserving idealist agent-features while declaring matter prius.

concepts.label: Adequate idea / active idea (Burke's Spinozist Marxism)
concepts.gloss: An idea is 'active' insofar as 'adequate' — i.e., insofar as it accurately names the malign and benign properties of the society in question. Inadequate ideas → social passions. Burke's Spinozist-translated Marxist motivation-table.

concepts.label: Actus / status / property (class-substantive triplet)
concepts.gloss: Each class is distinct in actus (way of life as acted), hence in status (way of life as positioned), hence in properties (characteristics, possessions, ways of speaking/thinking). Burke imports GM-02 substance-vocabulary into Marxism's reconstruction.

concepts.label: Monad as atom-agent (Leibnizian)
concepts.gloss: Leibnizian monad = substance with internal principle of self-development, particular point of view, range from implicit to explicit. Anticipates psychologies of the unconscious. Pre-established harmony solves the no-windows problem of inter-monadic coordination.

concepts.label: Problem of the intrinsic (things-without-context)
concepts.gloss: Grammatically: as soon as things are considered in relation to other things, one is on the way to dissolving them into their context. Things-in-themselves = things-without-relation. Leibniz's pre-established harmony as ingenious metaphysical solution; Spinoza's totality-substance as alternative.

concepts.label: Imagination (idealist-scientist cluster term)
concepts.gloss: Modern cult of imagination as agent-of-creative-poetic-cognition; Coleridge from Kant; Wallace Stevens's deployment in personality / nervous sensitiveness / sensation / temperament cluster. Ironic finding: pro-poetry imagination-cult inherits scientist-idealist patterning.

concepts.label: Externalization / pattern of inner-to-outer
concepts.gloss: Post-Fichte idealist pattern: nature as externalization or expression of spirit — implicit to explicit, unconscious to conscious, magma to lava, visceral to excretory. Schelling aesthetic, Hegel optimistic, Schopenhauer pessimistic variants of one externalization-pattern.

concepts.label: Four realms of being (Santayana)
concepts.gloss: Matter / essence / spirit / truth. Matter = scene of flux; essence = appearance considered in itself, eternal possibility, indelible background; spirit = moral fruition of physical life; truth = essences embodied in factual world.

concepts.label: Scribe-script-scroll pattern (Avicebron / Santayana)
concepts.gloss: Avicebron's Fons Vitae: scene=matter (scroll), act=form (script), agent=will (scribe). Santayana's variant: scroll = realm of essence; script-and-scribe combined = existence selecting one line of possibilities. Pentad-mapped pattern with idealist-aesthetic re-tuning.

concepts.label: Volonté générale / consubstantial founder-will (Rousseau, US Constitution)
concepts.gloss: Idealistic ground for legal motive: positive law derives from assemblies enacting 'the will of the people'; US fiction that present-will is consubstantial with founder-will. Document as ground of action whose essential feature is derivation from agent-attitudes.

concepts.label: Scientism pervading modern idealism
concepts.gloss: Burke's diagnostic finding: modern idealist vocabularies, from Berkeley forward, are scientistically inflected — Hume's pure-empiricism is one face; Kant's epistemological-constitutive realm is another; even the cult of imagination as 'truer kind of truth' inherits the scientist pattern. Idealism + scientism are paired.

agent_term_operationalization.definition: Agent is the pentad term that names the doer of any act — the constituting subject from which, in idealist construal, motive originates. Idealism features Agent by deriving scene, act, agency, and purpose from properties of the agent; non-idealist construals deploy Agent without featuring it. The term answers 'Who?' and its derivatives.
agent_term_operationalization.question_answered: Who? (Who did it? Whose act is this? In whose consciousness, by which mind, by which subject?)

paradigm_examples_from_burke.label: ego / self / super-ego / consciousness / will / generalized I
soul / spirit / oversoul / mind
paradigm_examples_from_burke.note: Religious-mystical inflections of the same agent-vocabulary

paradigm_examples_from_burke.label: super-persons: church, race, nation, historical period treated as personality
Kantian universalized agent / 'the understanding' in general
paradigm_examples_from_burke.note: Agent universalized beyond your-mine to attain objective necessity

paradigm_examples_from_burke.label: Marxist class as collective agent
paradigm_examples_from_burke.note: Hybrid case — class-as-bearer-of-actus-status-properties grounds motive structurally even under materialist surface

paradigm_examples_from_burke.label: Hegelian Spirit / World-Historical Hero
paradigm_examples_from_burke.note: Universal Agent realizing itself through subjective passions via cunning of Reason

paradigm_examples_from_burke.label: Santayana's spirit as moral fruition of physical life

agent_term_operationalization.philosophic_school: idealism (with Marxism as hybrid scene-grounded-but-agent-featuring extension)
decision_rules_for_ambiguous_cases: If scenic features (environment, conditions, material context) are explicitly DERIVED FROM properties of a subject/mind/consciousness/spirit/will (rather than the reverse), the locus is Agent.

If a putative material/scenic ground turns out, under analysis, to be a 'super-agent' (God as Almighty Agent, Spirit, Nation-Will, Class-Consciousness, Universal Reason), the locus is Agent, not Scene.
If the philosophy treats consciousness/idea/concept/sensation as PRIMARY and matter as derivative, secondary, or unnecessary hypothesis (Berkeley), the locus is Agent.

If the philosophy preserves a materialist surface but smuggles agenthood into matter itself (Lenin's property-similar-to-sensation; Spinoza's parallelism), the locus is Agent-and-Scene hybrid — diagnose by which term is the GROUND of derivation.

If a collective agent (class, party, race, nation) is the bearer of properties (actus, status, ways of life, consciousness), the locus is Agent even where materialist vocabulary dominates the rhetoric.

Distinguish AGENT from AGENCY: Agent answers 'Who?', Agency answers 'By what means / instrument?' A controller is Agency; the player who wields it is Agent; the avatar through which the player acts is also Agent (with a shifting-Agent ratio Burke would call agent-act in operation).

When the philosophy reduces inquiry to 'the problem of knowledge' (epistemology as first philosophy), the locus is Agent — because epistemology grounds speculation psychologistically, in the nature of the knower.
agent_term_operationalization.calleja_pim_mapping: Shared dimension + the avatar/character question (who is acting — player-as-self? avatar? character-in-narrative? when does the agent-position shift?). Anticipatory, dissertation-projected.
agent_term_operationalization.uexkull_mapping: Subject-of-functional-circle / Innenwelt (the perceiving-acting subject as inner-world bearer whose Merken and Wirken close the loop with Umwelt). Anticipatory, dissertation-projected — flag risk of forcing the parallel since Uexküll is biosemiotic-objectivist where Burke is dramatistic-rhetorical.
agent_term_operationalization.ontological_grounding_candidate: Aristotelian psuchē (soul as the principle of life and action; De Anima's hylomorphic-psyche; psuchē as proximate ground of orexis, phantasia, and praxis) + Heideggerian Dasein (being-for-which-its-own-being-is-an-issue; the entity whose mode of being is existence) — both flagged ANTICIPATORY (Burke 1945 predates the English-language reception of Heidegger by 17 years; psuchē-Burke bridge is anticipatory because Burke does not himself anchor Agent in De Anima, though GM-06 anchors Act in Aristotle exegetically).
agent_term_operationalization.forward_reference_to_rhetoric_of_motives: When the Rhetoric of Motives pipeline is built, Agent's operational entry must add Attitude as 6th term and incorporate consubstantiation / identification — the rhetorical mechanism by which Agent-positions merge, share substance, and identify with other Agents. Pre-allocated field; pending-future-rhetoric-of-motives-pipeline.

philosophic_school_mapping.burke_diagnostic: Idealism is recognized by featuring Agent as motive-locus: scene, act, agency, and purpose are derived from properties of the constituting subject (mind, ego, consciousness, will, spirit, super-agent). The philosophical idiom is recognizable not by which terms it uses but by which it features as ground.

per_philosopher_table.burke_move: Treats Berkeley as the cleanest idealist exhibit. Berkeley begins psychologistically (Lockean abstract-idea critique), reduces objects to ideas (esse is percipi), reduces matter to unnecessary hypothesis (reversed Occamite parsimony), grounds active principle in mind/spirit/soul, and routes residual scene-function through God as 'Almighty Agent.' The strategy is ITSELF the operationalization of Agent: every scenic remainder gets translated into terms of super-agent.

Transitional figure who narrows Berkeleian idealism's circumference by equating ideas with sensations and dropping the rationalist/intelligible side, focusing on what laboratory investigation can handle. Dismantles causality/power/necessary connection as empirically un-derivable. The 'great dramatist cluster' (reason, substance, cause, necessity, action, idea, God, Nature, generation, power) begins to fall apart — but the move is itself agent-featuring because the dismantling proceeds by reflecting on 'operations of our own minds.'

Rationalism of idealist cast — monad as atom-agent with internal self-development, perception-slanted substance, pre-established harmony solving the no-windows coordination problem via God as Monas Monadum. Anticipates modern psychologies of the unconscious. Provides Kant the Leibnizian unification-pressure that Hume's skepticism leaves no room for.

The dominant idealism interlocutor of the chapter. Burke reconstructs Kant as solving Hume's medium-demand by equating medium with universalized agent: 'the understanding' is the locus of categories; agent supplies the conditions of possibility of experience. Transcendental logic generates a scene-narrowed-to-motion derived from agent's nature; transcendent realm (things-in-themselves, unconditioned, freedom) added by Coleridgean desynonymizing of transcendental/transcendent, providing ground for moral action via als-ob ideas of God/freedom/immortality. The constitution-enactment analogy is Burke's gloss on the freedom-necessity bridge.

World History as development of Spirit through embodiment in historical detail; cunning of Reason mechanism (Spirit acts through subjective human passions); State as Divine Idea on earth; World-Historical Hero close to fountainhead of Spirit. Hegel deepens Kant's concrete-conditions treatment by mediating Spirit through nature and history, providing a super-agent whose vehicle is a graded sequence of historical-cultural agents.

The hybrid case — Marxism grows out of idealism BY ANTITHESIS (Hegel inverted, matter as prius, consciousness derivative). Surface vocabulary is materialist; structural motive-locus is class-as-collective-agent. Burke argues: (i) dialectical materialism, being dialectical, requires 'some quality of agenthood permeating the scene itself' (Lenin's property-similar-to-sensation in matter); (ii) Marxism's futuristic stress on social unification + constant call upon human agents = intensely idealistic; (iii) class is bearer of actus, status, properties — a Spinozist-translated-into-class-terms agent-substance; (iv) the Manifesto AS act of propaganda performs Agent-feature even while its rhetoric reflects-conditions. Burke's verdict: 'idealistic materialist.'

philosophic_school_mapping.marxism_nuance_note: Burke's most distinctive contribution in GM-05 is the careful capture of Marxism's hybrid character. Marxism is NOT classed simply as a fifth idealism; it is treated as an extension/inversion of Hegelian idealism in which the scenic-grounding rhetoric carries an agent-featuring substructure. The diagnostic is that Marxism's class-as-collective-agent + adequate-idea / active-idea / class-consciousness vocabulary + Manifesto-as-propaganda-act-presupposing-ideas-as-social-forces all require the philosophy to be read, in Burke's Grammar, as Agent-featuring under a materialist surface — best translated as 'idealistic materialist.' This is also why GM-05 (Agent in General) is the locus for the Marxism subsections rather than GM-04 (Scene-as-materialism).

positions.claim: Idealism features Agent as motive-locus: the constituting subject (mind, ego, consciousness, will, spirit, super-agent) is the originating ground from which scene, act, agency, and purpose are derived.
positions.argument_form: Diagnostic: the cluster of agent-vocabulary across idealist thinkers (Berkeley, Hume, Leibniz, Kant, Fichte, Schelling, Hegel, Schopenhauer) consistently locates motive in agent-side terms.

positions.claim: Whenever a philosophy treats 'the problem of knowledge' as first philosophy, it grounds speculation psychologistically — in the nature of the knower — and is therefore Agent-featuring regardless of its self-description.
positions.argument_form: Conditional: epistemology-as-first-philosophy entails agent-as-ground (because epistemology asks 'how is knowledge possible?' which routes inquiry through the knowing-subject).

positions.claim: Marxism is best translated as 'idealistic materialist': despite materialist surface vocabulary, its motive-locus is the class-as-collective-agent, and its futuristic stress on social unification + constant call upon human agents is intensely idealistic.
positions.argument_form: Hybrid diagnosis: dialectical materialism, being dialectical and not vulgar, requires agenthood permeating scene (Lenin's sensation-in-matter); class as bearer of actus/status/properties is the agent-substructure; Manifesto-as-propaganda-act performs Agent-feature even while reflecting-conditions rhetorically.

positions.claim: Kant resolves Hume's demand for a medium (to explain inference from observed-sequence to causal-necessity) by equating the medium with the universalized agent itself, relocating causality from scene to agent's nature.
positions.argument_form: Reconstruction: Hume's empiricism cannot anchor causality in observation; Kant's transcendental move (universalize agent → 'the understanding' → categories of unification → space and time as forms of sensibility) places the conditions of necessity in agent. This generates a scene-narrowed-to-motion derived from agent.

positions.claim: Modern idealist vocabularies (from Berkeley forward, especially Kant and the post-Kantian inheritances in Coleridge's and Stevens's imagination-cult) carry a scientist bias — even the pro-poetry imagination-against-science move inherits the patterning it would reject.
positions.argument_form: Genealogical: Stevens's imagination-cluster (personality, sensation, temperament) inherits via Coleridge from Kant; Shelley's poetry-as-centre-and-circumference traces backward through Leibniz to Pascal to Rabelais, drifting scientist as it approaches modernity.

positions.claim: The intrinsic (transcendent in Kant; thing-in-itself; monad-without-windows in Leibniz; essence in Santayana) is Grammatically the realm of things-without-context, things-without-relation — hence of the unconditioned, hence of freedom.
positions.argument_form: Grammatical: relations are determinations (termini); a thing considered apart from context is undetermined; the undetermined is the unconditioned; the unconditioned is the realm of freedom. Pentad-grammatical re-mapping of the metaphysics of substance.

positions.claim: Santayana's materialism — like Marxism's — grows antithetically out of German transcendentalism and is more explicit than Marxism in stressing the material basis of spiritual fulfilment; yet his doctrine of essence locates an idealist core (essences as eternal contemplable possibilities) inside the materialist frame.
positions.argument_form: Parallel-construction: just as Marxism is idealistic-materialist via class-as-agent + adequate-idea, so Santayana is idealistic-materialist via essence-as-eternal-possibility + spirit-as-moral-fruition-of-physical-life. The two cases are not identical (Marxist urgency vs. Santayanan retirement) but structurally parallel.

tensions.tension: The Communist Manifesto's scenic-reflection rhetoric (man's consciousness changes with man's material conditions; ideas-merely-express-class-fact) is in tension with the Manifesto's performative act-of-propaganda character (which presupposes ideas as social forces, ideas-as-changers-of-conditions).
tensions.resolution_burke: Burke's resolution: Marxism IS idealistic-materialist; the tension is a feature, not a bug — class-as-collective-agent grounds motive structurally even where surface vocabulary inverts the genealogy. The Manifesto's act-of-propaganda performance is structurally Agent-featuring.

tensions.tension: Kant's transcendental synthesis is called 'spontaneous' and 'original' (active-action of the mind) but it is also 'inevitable' (the mind cannot see otherwise than in terms of the categories), lacking the elements of freedom necessary for genuine moral action.
tensions.resolution_burke: Burke notes Kant resolves this only by ADDING a third realm (transcendent / things-in-themselves / unconditioned) where genuine freedom resides. The transcendental-active is constitutive (scene-narrowed-to-motion); the transcendent-free is regulative (idea-of-action). The als-ob principle bridges.

tensions.tension: Santayana is overtly materialist (matter is scene, animal-faith posits material world, spirit grounded materialistically) yet his doctrine of essence locates an idealist core: essences as eternal possibilities, intuited directly, contemplated apart from existence, ultimately a thanatopsis.
tensions.resolution_burke: Burke: this is structurally parallel to Marxism's idealistic-materialism. Both materialisms grow antithetically out of German transcendentalism; both preserve an agent-featuring core (class-as-agent for Marx; spirit-as-fruition + essence-as-contemplable for Santayana).

tensions.tension: The modern cult of imagination is urged by champions of poetry-against-science (Stevens, Coleridge, Shelley) yet inherits scientist patterning via the very idealist genealogy (Kant → Coleridge → Stevens) it would deploy against science.
tensions.resolution_burke: Burke does not dissolve the tension; he diagnoses it as the typical idealist-scientist scientism-permeating-modern-thought finding. The 'correct controversy' is not art-against-science but one-view-of-science against another (dramatistic-rhetorical vs. positivist-empirical).

tensions.tension: Kant's resolution to Hume requires universalizing agent (not your-understanding or mine but 'the understanding'); but this universalization risks emptying agent of agency — the universal-understanding cannot 'do' anything in the moral-action sense.
tensions.resolution_burke: Burke notes this is one reason Kant needs the transcendent realm: only there can the universal-agent-substructure issue in particular moral acts grounded in the noumenal will. Fichte's later move (abolish thing-in-itself, ground everything in Ego) intensifies the tension by absorbing all particularity into a still-more-universal Ego/Non-Ego dialectic.

ratio_deployments.deployment: Berkeley's reduction of objects to ideas inverts the materialist scene-agent: instead of scene-grounding-agent, agent-grounds-scene (esse is percipi; matter as unnecessary hypothesis).

Burke's Spinozist-translated Marxist motivation-table: an idea is 'active' insofar as 'adequate'; adequate ideas under-write active (revolutionary) acts; inadequate ideas yield social passions. Agent-act ratio at the class-level.
The Manifesto deploys scene-agent materialistically — 'every change in the conditions' of man's material existence is accompanied by change in 'man's ideas, views, and conceptions.'

Moral motive as bond between realm of necessity and realm of freedom; ideas of God / freedom / immortality as regulative principles by which agent acts as-if toward purposes that cannot be known empirically. Mechanism-in-nature as sign of purpose-behind-nature.

Coleridge's desynonymizing operation as the agent's strategic management of agency (linguistic-conceptual tools); Burke notes the strategic-synonymizing/desynonymizing operation as a meta-move of the philosophical agent over the philosophical agency.

Lenin smuggles agenthood into scene: 'property similar to sensation in foundation stones of the structure of matter itself' — preserving dialectical-materialist scene-priority while permitting agent-features in matter.
